_schema._about: Topographia Sacra · canonical gazetteer across all books in the series. Each entry is a place named in scripture, keyed by a stable lowercase slug. Edit this file to revise identifications across the whole series; chapter pages read from it at load.

fields.name: Display name (English form, as used by Anchor Bible Dictionary)
fields.name_alt: Alternative names or transliterations, optional, for search/index
fields.coords: [latitude, longitude] of the leading identification, decimal degrees, WGS84
fields.alternatives: Optional array of {site, source} for disputed identifications; cite footnote in chapter data
fields.appearances: Array of {book, chapter, verses} where the place is named

tier_meanings.conjectural: Best guess, multiple candidates, or general region only
tier_meanings.unknown: Named but unlocatable; should NOT appear on a map — list only in gazetteer
tier_meanings.region: Approximate region only; pin sits at the regional center with distinctive faint dashed styling, popup notes 'no specific site identified'.

jericho.name: Jericho
jericho.id: Tell es-Sultan, on the western edge of the Jordan Valley c. 10 km NW of the Dead Sea. Excavated by Sellin & Watzinger, Garstang, Kenyon, and most recently by the Italian–Palestinian expedition.

gilgal.name: Gilgal
gilgal.id: Israelite encampment east of Jericho near the Jordan. Several candidates have been proposed in the plain between Tell es-Sultan and the river; no site has produced decisive evidence.

jordan.name: The Jordan
jordan.id: The Jordan River; the crossing point in the Joshua narrative is traditionally placed opposite Jericho near the el-Maghtas ford, modern Qasr el-Yahud.

ai.name: Ai
ai.id: A fortified site east of Bethel in the central hill country. The traditional identification is et-Tell ("the mound"), excavated by Marquet-Krause and Callaway, but the site shows no Late Bronze occupation, prompting alternative proposals.

alternatives.source: Albright; Callaway (traditional consensus, but stratigraphy problematic)
Bryant Wood / Associates for Biblical Research

bethel.name: Bethel
bethel.id: Beitin, a village c. 17 km north of Jerusalem on the central ridge route. Identified by Edward Robinson (1838) and excavated by Albright and Kelso. Earlier called Luz (Joshua 18:13).

beth-aven.name: Beth-aven
beth-aven.id: A site "east of Bethel" in the Joshua narrative, used as a directional landmark. Possibly identical with later Beth-el itself (so Hosea 4:15) or a now-lost site between Bethel and Ai. No archaeological identification has been confirmed.

shebarim.name: Shebarim
shebarim.id: Mentioned only as the place to which Israel was pursued from Ai (Joshua 7:5). The Hebrew may be a common noun ("the quarries" or "the shattered places") rather than a place name; if a place, it is unlocated.

valley-of-achor.name: Valley of Achor
valley-of-achor.id: A wadi on the route between Jericho and the central hill country, named for the "trouble" (Hebrew 'akar) caused by Achan. Most often identified with the Wadi Qelt or the Buqei'ah valley west of Jericho; the precise location is debated.

shittim.name: Shittim
shittim.id: The Israelite encampment in the plains of Moab east of the Jordan, c. 12 km ENE of Jericho. No site has been archaeologically confirmed; the leading candidates are Tell el-Hammam and Tell el-Kefrein, both on the well-watered plain north of the Dead Sea.

adam.name: Adam
adam.id: Tell ed-Damiyeh, on the east bank of the Jordan near the mouth of the Jabbok, c. 25 km north of Jericho. The identification is secure on linguistic and topographic grounds; the site sits at a constriction in the Jordan corridor where landslide damming of the river has been historically attested.

zarethan.name: Zarethan
zarethan.id: An unconfirmed site in the Jordan Valley, named here as the city beside Adam. The leading candidate is Tell es-Saʿidiyeh, c. 28 km north of Jericho on the east bank; Tell Umm Hamad has also been proposed.

dead-sea.name: The Dead Sea
dead-sea.id: The salt lake at the southern end of the Jordan Rift Valley, c. 80 km long, the lowest point on the earth's surface (−430 m). Called the “Salt Sea” and the “sea of the Arabah” in the Hebrew Bible. Forms the eastern boundary of Judah and the western boundary of Moab.

mount-ebal.name: Mount Ebal
mount-ebal.id: The northern of the two mountains flanking Shechem (modern Nablus), 940 m above sea level. Site of Joshua's altar and the inscription of the law in the MT, LXX, and Vulgate; the Samaritan Pentateuch and 4QJosh^a place the altar on Mount Gerizim instead.

mount-gerizim.name: Mount Gerizim
mount-gerizim.id: The southern of the two mountains flanking Shechem (modern Nablus), 881 m above sea level. The Samaritan holy mountain, site of a Samaritan temple from the Persian period; the Samaritan Pentateuch's reading of Deuteronomy 27:4 places Joshua's altar here rather than on Mount Ebal.

gibeon.name: Gibeon
gibeon.id: el-Jib, c. 9 km NW of Jerusalem on the central ridge route. Identified by Edward Robinson (1838); Pritchard's excavations later recovered jar handles inscribed gbʿn (Gibeon), confirming the identification beyond reasonable doubt.

chephirah.name: Chephirah
chephirah.id: Khirbet el-Kefira (also Kefireh), c. 11 km W of Jerusalem on a ridge above the Wadi Qatrun. One of the four Hivite/Gibeonite cities. Iron Age occupation has been confirmed by survey.

beeroth.name: Beeroth
beeroth.id: Identification disputed. The traditional candidate is el-Bireh, just N of Ramallah; alternatives include Khirbet el-Burj near Tell el-Ful and Nebi Samwil.

kiriath-jearim.name: Kiriath Jearim
kiriath-jearim.id: Tell el-Azhar (Deir el-Azhar), c. 13 km W of Jerusalem on the central ridge route. Identified by Robinson and confirmed by excavation; the Iron Age site sits directly atop a Bronze Age tell.

jerusalem.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

hebron.name: Hebron
hebron.id: Tel Rumeida (within modern Hebron / al-Khalil), in the Judean hill country c. 30 km SSW of Jerusalem. The patriarchal city of the Cave of Machpelah; king Hoham named here as a southern coalition member.

jarmuth.name: Jarmuth
jarmuth.id: Tel Yarmut (Khirbet Yarmuk), in the Shephelah c. 25 km W of Jerusalem. A major Early Bronze and Late Bronze fortified site, identified by Robinson and confirmed by recent excavations.

lachish.name: Lachish
lachish.id: Tel Lachish (Tell ed-Duweir), the largest mound in the Shephelah, c. 40 km SW of Jerusalem. Identified by Albright; thoroughly excavated. The Late Bronze destruction layer (Stratum VII / VI) sits awkwardly with the conquest narrative — see footnote.

eglon.name: Eglon
eglon.id: Identification disputed. Tell el-Hesi (Petrie/Bliss) was the older candidate; Tell Aitun / Khirbet ʿAjlan, c. 8 km W of Lachish, is now generally favored. The pin marks Tell Aitun.

beth-horon.name: Beth Horon
beth-horon.id: Two villages on the ascent from the Aijalon Valley to the central hill country: Upper Beth Horon (Beit ʿUr al-Foqa, 617 m) and Lower Beth Horon (Beit ʿUr al-Tahta, 400 m), c. 2 km apart. The pin marks the upper village; the “ascent of Beth Horon” is the road between them.

azekah.name: Azekah
azekah.id: Tell Zakariyeh, in the Shephelah overlooking the Elah Valley, c. 25 km SW of Jerusalem. A prominent fortified site through the Iron Age; identified by Robinson.

makkedah.name: Makkedah
makkedah.id: Identification disputed. Khirbet el-Qom (c. 13 km W of Hebron) and Khirbet Beit Maqdum have both been proposed. The pin marks Khirbet el-Qom.

valley-of-aijalon.name: The Valley of Aijalon
valley-of-aijalon.id: The broad valley running east-west between the central ridge and the Shephelah, named for the village of Aijalon (modern Yalo). The natural corridor from the coastal plain to the hill country, the valley is the locus of v.12’s “Sun, stand still on Gibeon; you, moon, in the valley of Aijalon.”

libnah.name: Libnah
libnah.id: Identification disputed. Tel Burna (Tell Bornat) in the Shephelah is the leading current candidate; Tell es-Safi was earlier proposed but has now been identified as Gath, removing it from contention.

alternatives.source: older proposals — now identified as Gath

gezer.name: Gezer
gezer.id: Tel Gezer, on the northern edge of the Shephelah c. 30 km W of Jerusalem. A major Bronze and Iron Age site; the identification was secured by inscribed boundary stones recovered by Macalister.

debir.name: Debir
debir.id: Khirbet Rabud, in the southern Judean hill country c. 12 km SW of Hebron. Identified by Kochavi against the older Albright proposal of Tell Beit Mirsim, which lacked the necessary water source and Late Bronze occupation profile.

kadesh-barnea.name: Kadesh Barnea
kadesh-barnea.id: ʿAin Qudeirat, the largest spring in the northern Sinai / Negev frontier, c. 80 km SW of Beersheba. The Israelite encampment of Numbers 13–14 and the southernmost reach of the conquest in v.41.

gaza.name: Gaza
gaza.id: The southernmost of the five Philistine pentapolis cities, on the coastal plain c. 80 km SW of Jerusalem. The west-coast extreme of the southern campaign’s reach in v.41.

goshen-of-judah.name: Goshen (of Judah)
goshen-of-judah.id: Distinct from the Egyptian Goshen of Genesis–Exodus. A region in the southern Shephelah / Judean foothills, sometimes identified with the area around Tell el-Khuweilfeh; precise extent unknown.

hazor.name: Hazor
hazor.id: Tell el-Qedah, the largest mound in the southern Levant (c. 200 acres), in the Huleh basin of upper Galilee. The Bronze Age regional capital, named in Egyptian execration texts and the Mari archives; identified by Garstang and excavated by Yadin and Ben-Tor.

madon.name: Madon
madon.id: Identification disputed. Qarn Hattin / Khirbet Madin (the Horns of Hattin) is the traditional candidate; Tel Madin and other sites in lower Galilee have been proposed.

shimron.name: Shimron
shimron.id: Tell Shimron (Khirbet Sammuniyeh), c. 8 km W of Nazareth on the southern edge of the Beth Netofa valley. A major Late Bronze and Iron Age fortified site.

achshaph.name: Achshaph
achshaph.id: Identification disputed. Tell Keisan in the Acco plain is the leading current candidate; Tell el-Harbaj and other sites have been proposed.

chinneroth.name: Chinneroth
name_alt: Sea of Chinneroth (= Sea of Galilee)
chinneroth.id: Tel Kinrot (Tell el-Oreimeh) on the NW shore of the Sea of Galilee. The name also designates the lake itself in the Hebrew Bible (the Sea of Chinneroth, later Lake Gennesaret).

dor.name: Dor
dor.id: Tel Dor on the Mediterranean coast, c. 30 km S of Haifa. A major harbor town through the Bronze and Iron Ages; identified securely by name continuity and confirmed by excavation.

mount-hermon.name: Mount Hermon
mount-hermon.id: The southern peak of the anti-Lebanon range, 2,814 m above sea level — the highest point in the region. Marks the northern boundary of Israelite territorial claims in the conquest narrative.

merom.name: The Waters of Merom
merom.id: Identification debated. The traditional view places the waters at Lake Hula in the upper Jordan valley; more recent proposals identify Merom with Meron (Tell Meron) in upper Galilee, with the “waters” being a nearby spring or wadi.

sidon.name: Sidon
sidon.id: Modern Saida on the Lebanese coast, c. 40 km S of Beirut. A major Phoenician city through the Bronze and Iron Ages; named in this chapter as the northwestern reach of the Israelite pursuit ("great Sidon").

misrephoth-maim.name: Misrephoth Maim
misrephoth-maim.id: Identification uncertain. Khirbet el-Mishrefeh on the coast S of Tyre is the leading candidate; the Hebrew name ("burnings of waters") may refer to hot springs in the area.

mount-halak.name: Mount Halak
mount-halak.id: The "Smooth Mountain," named as the southern boundary of Israelite conquest. Identification not settled; Jebel Halaq in the Negev highlands is the traditional candidate.

baal-gad.name: Baal Gad
baal-gad.id: A site "in the valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon," named as the northern boundary of conquest. Identification disputed; candidates include sites in the upper Beqa valley, with Hasbaya and the area around Banias most often proposed.

anab.name: Anab
anab.id: Khirbet ʿAnab, c. 18 km SSW of Hebron in the southern Judean hill country. One of the cities purged of the Anakim by Joshua.

gath.name: Gath
gath.id: Tell es-Safi, in the Shephelah on the eastern edge of the coastal plain. The largest of the Philistine pentapolis cities by the Iron Age; long misidentified, then secured by Bunimovitz and Maeir's recent excavations.

ashdod.name: Ashdod
ashdod.id: Tell Ashdod, c. 6 km inland from the Mediterranean. One of the five Philistine pentapolis cities; identified securely on the basis of toponymic continuity.

heshbon.name: Heshbon
heshbon.id: Tell Hesban, on the plateau east of the Dead Sea c. 25 km SW of Amman. The traditional identification, though excavation has shown only minimal Late Bronze occupation — Sihon's kingdom, like Ai, sits awkwardly with the available stratigraphy.

ashtaroth.name: Ashtaroth
ashtaroth.id: Tell Ashtarah in the Hauran of southern Syria, c. 35 km E of the Sea of Galilee. The royal city of Og of Bashan; identified on the basis of Egyptian texts (the Anastasi Papyri) and the Amarna letters.

arnon.name: The Arnon
arnon.id: Wadi Mujib, the canyon-like river system that empties into the eastern shore of the Dead Sea. Forms the historical boundary between Moab to the south and the kingdom of Sihon to the north.

aroer.name: Aroer
aroer.id: Khirbet ʿArair, on the north rim of the Arnon canyon. Identified by Robinson and confirmed by excavation; multiple Aroers exist in the OT, but the toponym + canyon-edge geography is decisive here.

jabbok.name: The Jabbok
jabbok.id: Wadi Zarqa, the major eastern tributary of the Jordan, joining it c. 40 km N of the Dead Sea. Named here as the boundary between the kingdoms of Sihon (Heshbon) and the Ammonites.

beth-jeshimoth.name: Beth Jeshimoth
beth-jeshimoth.id: Tell el-ʿAzeimeh, on the NE shore of the Dead Sea opposite Jericho. Identification probable but not confirmed by excavation.

pisgah.name: Pisgah
pisgah.id: The ridge above the Plains of Moab, including Mount Nebo (Ras es-Siyaghah / Jebel Siyagha) — Moses' viewpoint over the land in Deuteronomy 34. The "slopes of Pisgah" descend westward toward the Dead Sea.

edrei.name: Edrei
edrei.id: Modern Daraa in southern Syria, on the historic Damascus-Amman road. One of the two royal cities of Og of Bashan, alongside Ashtaroth.

salecah.name: Salecah
salecah.id: Modern Salkhad on the southern slopes of Jebel Druze in the Hauran. The toponym is preserved continuously; Iron Age occupation has been confirmed.

geder.name: Geder
geder.id: Named only in Joshua 12:13, with no other biblical attestation and no proposed identification with extant remains. The Hebrew is a common noun ("wall" / "enclosure"), and some have argued the verse names a topographic feature rather than a city.

hormah.name: Hormah
hormah.id: Identification disputed. Tel Masos (in the Beersheba basin) and Tel Halif have both been proposed; the older identification with Tell esh-Sheriah is now generally rejected.

arad.name: Arad
arad.id: Tel Arad in the eastern Negev, c. 30 km E of Beersheba. Securely identified, but excavation has shown no Late Bronze occupation — the conquest narrative for Arad sits in the same stratigraphic difficulty as Ai and Heshbon.

adullam.name: Adullam
adullam.id: Tel ʿAdullam (Khirbet esh-Sheikh Madhkur), in the Shephelah c. 25 km SW of Jerusalem. Better known as the cave-refuge of David in 1 Samuel 22.

tappuah.name: Tappuah
tappuah.id: Sheikh Abu Zarad, in the central hill country c. 13 km SSW of Shechem. Identification on toponymic and geographic grounds; Iron Age occupation confirmed by survey.

hepher.name: Hepher
hepher.id: Identification disputed. Tell el-Muḥaffar in the western Jezreel hills is one current proposal; other sites have been suggested.

aphek.name: Aphek
aphek.id: Tel Aphek (Tell Ras el-ʿAin), at the headwaters of the Yarkon in the Sharon plain. Multiple Apheks appear in the OT — see footnote — but this listing in Joshua 12 is most often identified with the Sharon site.

lasharon.name: Lasharon
lasharon.id: Named only in Joshua 12:18, with no other biblical attestation. Some scholars take the Hebrew as a corruption of "to Sharon" (the coastal region) rather than a place name; the LXX appears to read it as a description of Aphek.

taanach.name: Taanach
taanach.id: Tell Taʿannak, on the southern edge of the Jezreel valley c. 8 km SE of Megiddo. A major Late Bronze and Iron Age site; identified by toponym and confirmed by excavation.

megiddo.name: Megiddo
megiddo.id: Tel Megiddo, the great mound on the southwestern edge of the Jezreel valley controlling the Aruna pass. One of the most thoroughly excavated sites in Israel; named in Egyptian, Assyrian, and biblical texts.

kedesh.name: Kedesh
kedesh.id: Tell Qades, in upper Galilee c. 15 km NW of Hazor. Multiple Kedeshes exist; the Joshua 12 listing is identified with Kedesh-Naphtali (cf. Joshua 19:37, 20:7) on the basis of geographic context.

jokneam.name: Jokneam
jokneam.id: Tell Qaymun, on the western edge of the Jezreel valley at the foot of Mount Carmel. Identified by toponym; confirmed by excavation.

mount-carmel.name: Mount Carmel
mount-carmel.id: The mountain ridge running c. 25 km NW from the Jezreel valley to the Mediterranean coast at modern Haifa. Named here as the locating context of Jokneam ("Jokneam in Carmel").

tirzah.name: Tirzah
tirzah.id: Tell el-Farʿah (North), c. 11 km NE of Shechem. Later the first capital of the northern kingdom of Israel before Omri's move to Samaria; identified securely by de Vaux.

shihor.name: Shihor
shihor.id: Most likely the Wadi El-Arish (the 'Brook of Egypt'), traditional southern boundary of Canaan; some have read it as a Nile branch east of the Delta. Pin marks the wadi mouth at the Mediterranean coast.

ekron.name: Ekron
ekron.id: Tel Miqne in the inner coastal plain. Identification confirmed by the seventh-century Ekron royal dedicatory inscription found in situ in 1996, naming the city and its kings.

ashkelon.name: Ashkelon
ashkelon.id: Tel Ashqelon on the Mediterranean coast, one of the five Philistine cities. Continuously occupied from the Bronze Age through the Crusader period; extensive excavation since 1985.

avvim.name: Avvim
avvim.id: Pre-Philistine inhabitants of the southern coastal plain ('villages as far as Gaza', Deut 2:23). No specific site; named here to round out the southern remnant.

mearah.name: Mearah
mearah.id: Unidentified. Hebrew mĕʿārâ ('cave'); often connected with Mughr/Maghara north of Sidon, but no firm site. Listed in the gazetteer for completeness.

aphek-of-amorites.name: Aphek (of the Amorites)
aphek-of-amorites.id: A northern Aphek 'on the border of the Amorites', distinct from the Sharon Aphek and from Aphek near Jezreel. Often identified with Afqa at the source of the Adonis (Nahr Ibrahim) in Lebanon; some prefer Tell Afaq southeast of Damascus.

gebal.name: Gebal
gebal.id: Byblos (modern Jbeil) on the Lebanese coast. Continuous occupation from the Neolithic; major Phoenician city. The 'Gebalites' here are its inhabitants, working stone for Solomon (1 Kgs 5:18).

lebanon-region.name: Lebanon
lebanon-region.id: The Lebanon range running parallel to the Mediterranean coast, north of Israel. Pin sits in the central range; the northern boundary of the promised land in this verse extends along its western flank.

lebo-hamath.name: Lebo Hamath
lebo-hamath.id: The northern frontier of the promised land, traditionally located at modern Lebweh (Lebo) in the northern Beqaa Valley, where the territory of Hamath began. The phrase 'entrance of Hamath' marks the watershed pass into the Orontes basin.

medeba.name: Medeba
medeba.id: Modern Madaba, Jordan, on the Mishor plateau. Continuous occupation; the Madaba Mosaic Map (sixth-century church floor) is housed there. Named here for the surrounding plain assigned to Reuben.

dibon.name: Dibon
dibon.id: Modern Dhiban, Jordan, north of the Arnon. Site of the Mesha Stele (ninth-century B.C.), which describes the Moabite king's recapture of the city. Iron Age fortifications excavated.

gilead.name: Gilead
gilead.id: The wooded highland east of the Jordan between the Yarmuk (north) and roughly the Heshbon plateau (south). 'Half of Gilead' is split between Gad and East-Manasseh in this chapter.

bashan.name: Bashan
bashan.id: Volcanic plateau east and northeast of the Sea of Chinnereth, corresponding roughly to the modern Hauran. Famous in the Hebrew Bible for its cattle and oaks. Allotted to East-Manasseh.

bamoth-baal.name: Bamoth Baal
bamoth-baal.id: Unidentified high-place site in Reuben's allotment. The name ('high places of Baal') suggests a cult installation; possibly the Bamoth of Num 21:19-20 near the slopes of Pisgah, but no firm location.

beth-baal-meon.name: Beth Baal Meon
beth-baal-meon.id: Generally identified with Khirbet Maʿin southwest of Madaba. The Mesha Stele attributes its rebuilding to the Moabite king, suggesting it was a fortified Moabite town in Iron II.

jahaz.name: Jahaz
jahaz.id: Probably Khirbet el-Medeiyineh on the Wadi eth-Themed, on the eastern edge of the Mishor. Disputed; other proposals include Khirbet Iskander. Site of the battle in which Sihon was defeated (Num 21:23).

kedemoth.name: Kedemoth
kedemoth.id: An eastern town of Reuben near the desert fringe; proposed sites include es-Saliyeh and Khirbet er-Remeil. The 'wilderness of Kedemoth' (Deut 2:26) lies just east of here.

mephaath.name: Mephaath
mephaath.id: Probably Tell Jawah south of Amman, or alternatively Khirbet Nefa'a; mentioned by Eusebius as a Roman garrison post against the desert.

kiriathaim.name: Kiriathaim
kiriathaim.id: A 'twin city' of Reuben, possibly Qaryat el-Mekhayyat west of Madaba near Mount Nebo; another candidate is Khirbet el-Qureiyat. The Mesha Stele names a Moabite Kiriathaim, presumably the same.

sibmah.name: Sibmah
sibmah.id: A Reubenite town near Heshbon, famed for its vineyards (Isa 16:8-9, Jer 48:32). Often identified with Khirbet Qarn el-Kibsh, but the location is not secure.

zereth-shahar.name: Zereth Shahar
zereth-shahar.id: Unidentified. The Hebrew suggests 'splendor of dawn'; located 'on the mount of the valley'. Some have proposed Zarat on the east Dead Sea shore, but the geographic indicator points to a hill site.

beth-peor.name: Beth Peor
beth-peor.id: A site on the slopes east of the Jordan opposite Jericho, near Pisgah; the burial place of Moses (Deut 34:6) is 'in the valley opposite Beth Peor'. Proposals cluster on the slopes of Mount Nebo (Khirbet ʿAyun Musa, Khirbet esh-Sheikh Jayil).

jazer.name: Jazer
jazer.id: Generally located at Khirbet Jazzir near es-Salt in northern Gilead, though Khirbet es-Sar has also been proposed. A Levitical city assigned to the Merarites; later Ammonite during the divided monarchy.

rabbah-ammon.name: Rabbah
rabbah-ammon.id: The Ammonite capital, modern Amman. The acropolis (Jebel al-Qalʿa) preserves continuous occupation from the Bronze Age. Renamed Philadelphia in the Hellenistic period.

ramath-mizpeh.name: Ramath Mizpeh
ramath-mizpeh.id: Often identified with Tell er-Rumeith further north, or with Khirbet Jelad or Tell Suf in central Gilead. May or may not be the same as Ramoth-gilead; the relationship is unsettled.

betonim.name: Betonim
betonim.id: Identified with Khirbet Batneh, southwest of es-Salt in central Gilead. The toponym preserves the ancient name.

mahanaim.name: Mahanaim
mahanaim.id: On the Jabbok in northern Gilead. Two adjacent mounds, Tell edh-Dhahab el-Gharbi (west) and el-Sharqi (east), are both candidates. A Levitical city; refuge of David during Absalom's revolt (2 Sam 17).

debir-east.name: Debir (eastern)
debir-east.id: An eastern Debir on Gad's border, distinct from the southern Debir (Khirbet Rabud) of Joshua 10–12. Possibly the same as Lo-debar (2 Sam 9:4) in Gilead, but the identification is not secure.

beth-haram.name: Beth Haram
beth-haram.id: A Jordan-valley town of Gad; candidates include Tell Iktanu and Tell er-Rama north of the Dead Sea. Later Hellenistic Livias/Julias.

beth-nimrah.name: Beth Nimrah
beth-nimrah.id: Generally identified with Tell Nimrin / Tell el-Bleibil on the Wadi Nimrin in the Jordan valley north of the Dead Sea. Toponym preserved in the wadi name.

succoth-east.name: Succoth
succoth-east.id: Tell Deir ʿAlla in the lower Jabbok / Jordan confluence area. Distinct from the Egyptian Succoth of the exodus narrative. Excavations have revealed a major Late Bronze and Iron Age sanctuary, including the Aramaic Balaam plaster text.

zaphon.name: Zaphon
zaphon.id: A Jordan-valley town of Gad. Candidates include Tell el-Mazar and Tell el-Qos on the east bank of the Jordan north of Succoth. Not to be confused with the mythological Mount Zaphon (Jebel al-Aqra) in northern Syria.

edom.name: Edom
edom.id: The territory south and southeast of the Dead Sea, ancestral homeland of Esau's descendants. Pin sits roughly at the heart of the Edomite plateau.

wilderness-of-zin.name: Wilderness of Zin
wilderness-of-zin.id: The desert tract south of the Negev highlands, between Kadesh-barnea and the Arabah. Distinct from the Wilderness of Sin further west.

ascent-of-akrabbim.name: Ascent of Akrabbim
ascent-of-akrabbim.id: A pass on the southern boundary of Judah / northern boundary of Edom. Often identified with Naqb es-Safa southwest of the Dead Sea, where the road climbs from the Arabah onto the Negev plateau.

hezron-judah.name: Hezron
hezron-judah.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Negev waypoints. A boundary point between Kadesh-barnea and Addar; not a clan-Hezron of Reuben.

addar.name: Addar
addar.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Negev waypoints.

karka.name: Karka
karka.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Negev waypoints.

azmon.name: Azmon
azmon.id: Often located at Ain el-Qaseimeh in the central Negev, on the line between Kadesh-barnea and the Brook of Egypt. Identification not secure.

beth-hoglah.name: Beth Hoglah
beth-hoglah.id: Generally located at Deir Hajla north of the Dead Sea, near the Jordan. The toponym is preserved in the Arabic name of the modern monastery.

beth-arabah.name: Beth Arabah
beth-arabah.id: A boundary site in the Jordan valley north of the Dead Sea, possibly Khirbet es-Sweisa or 'Ain el-Gharabeh. Listed twice (Josh 15:6 with Judah, 18:22 with Benjamin) — a true border town.

stone-of-bohan.name: Stone of Bohan
stone-of-bohan.id: A boundary marker — a stone associated with Bohan son of Reuben — between Beth Arabah and the ascent of Adummim. Location unknown.

ascent-of-adummim.name: Ascent of Adummim
ascent-of-adummim.id: The pass on the road from Jericho up to Jerusalem, traditionally Talat ed-Dam ('the bloody ascent') near the Khan al-Hatrura. The setting of the parable of the Good Samaritan in later tradition.

en-shemesh.name: En Shemesh
en-shemesh.id: The spring at 'Ain el-Hod (Ain Hawd) on the road between Jerusalem and Jericho, on the Judah/Benjamin border line.

en-rogel.name: En Rogel
en-rogel.id: Bir Ayyub ('Job's Well') below the confluence of the Kidron and Hinnom valleys at the southeast corner of ancient Jerusalem. The spring outside the city wall used as a meeting place in 2 Sam 17 and 1 Kgs 1.

valley-of-hinnom.name: Valley of Hinnom
valley-of-hinnom.id: The valley running south then east around the western and southern walls of the Old City of Jerusalem, modern Wadi er-Rababi. Site of the Topheth (Jer 7:31, 19:6) and the etymological source of Greek Gehenna.

valley-of-rephaim.name: Valley of Rephaim
valley-of-rephaim.id: The broad valley southwest of Jerusalem, traditionally the route of approach to the city from the coastal plain (2 Sam 5:18-22). Modern Baqa / Emek Refaim neighborhood preserves the name.

nephtoah.name: Waters of Nephtoah
nephtoah.id: The spring at Lifta on the northwest edge of modern Jerusalem. The name has been connected with Pharaoh Merneptah's spring mentioned in his stela.

mount-ephron.name: Mount Ephron
mount-ephron.id: A ridge between the Waters of Nephtoah and Kiriath Jearim; possibly the Beit Iksa / Beit Hanina massif west of Jerusalem. Not securely located.

mount-seir-judah.name: Mount Seir (northern)
mount-seir-judah.id: A hill west of Kiriath Jearim, distinct from the Edomite Mount Seir. Possibly the Saris ridge near modern Shoresh; identification not secure.

chesalon.name: Chesalon
chesalon.id: Modern Kesla west of Jerusalem, on the ridge identified as Mount Jearim in the boundary description.

beth-shemesh-judah.name: Beth Shemesh
beth-shemesh-judah.id: Tel Beit Shemesh / Tell er-Rumeileh in the Sorek Valley. Continuous excavation since 1911 has exposed Late Bronze and Iron Age levels; site of the return of the Ark in 1 Sam 6.

timnah-judah.name: Timnah
timnah-judah.id: Tel Batash in the Sorek Valley, excavated 1977-89. The Philistine Timnah of the Samson narratives (Judg 14). Distinct from the Negev Timnah of v. 57.

shikkeron.name: Shikkeron
shikkeron.id: A boundary point near Ekron; possibly Tell el-Ful (different from Saul's Gibeah of the same name) or Khirbet Sukreir. Not securely located.

mount-baalah.name: Mount Baalah
mount-baalah.id: An unidentified ridge between Shikkeron and Jabneel on the Mediterranean approach.

jabneel-judah.name: Jabneel
jabneel-judah.id: Tel Yavneh on the southern coastal plain. Distinct from the Galilean Jabneel of Naphtali (Josh 19:33). Later Hellenistic Jamnia, the Yavneh of post-70 rabbinic memory.

great-sea.name: Great Sea
great-sea.id: The Mediterranean. The standard western boundary of the promised land throughout Joshua. Pin sits in open water off the Carmel coast.

kiriath-sepher.name: Kiriath Sepher
kiriath-sepher.id: Earlier name of the southern Debir (Khirbet Rabud). The variant Kiriath Sannah appears at v. 49; both are pre-conquest names of the same town.

kabzeel.name: Kabzeel
kabzeel.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Negev (Judah's southern district).

eder.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Negev (Judah's southern district).

beersheba.name: Beersheba
beersheba.id: Tel Beersheba (Tell es-Saba) east of the modern city. Iron Age planned town with horned altar and water system; the southern anchor of the formula 'from Dan to Beersheba'.

ziklag.name: Ziklag
ziklag.id: Traditionally Tel Sera (Tell esh-Sharia); recent excavation at Khirbet a-Raʿi has been proposed as the better candidate, with eleventh-century B.C. destruction matching the David-Ziklag horizon (1 Sam 30). Pin marks Khirbet a-Raʿi.

eshtaol.name: Eshtaol
eshtaol.id: Generally located at modern Eshtaol / Ishwaʿ in the Sorek valley, paired with Zorah in the Samson narratives (Judg 13:25, 16:31).

zorah.name: Zorah
zorah.id: Tel Tzora (Saraa) overlooking the Sorek valley, paired with Eshtaol; home of Manoah and birthplace of Samson (Judg 13).

ashnah-1.name: Ashnah
ashnah-1.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Shephelah (Judah's lowland district).

zanoah-shephelah.name: Zanoah
zanoah-shephelah.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Shephelah (Judah's lowland district).

enam.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Shephelah (Judah's lowland district).

socoh-shephelah.name: Socoh
socoh-shephelah.id: Khirbet ʿAbbad / Khirbet Shuweiket overlooking the Elah valley. The Goliath narrative locates the Philistines 'between Socoh and Azekah' (1 Sam 17:1).

shaaraim.name: Shaaraim
shaaraim.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the Shephelah.

keilah.name: Keilah
keilah.id: Khirbet Qila on the Elah valley road. Site of David's relief of the city against the Philistines (1 Sam 23).

mareshah.name: Mareshah
mareshah.id: Tel Maresha in the southern Shephelah. Major Iron II town fortified by Rehoboam (2 Chr 11:8); later Hellenistic Marisa with painted tomb-chambers.

shamir.name: Shamir
shamir.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the hill country of Judah.

jattir.name: Jattir
jattir.id: Khirbet ʿAttir in the southern Hebron hills. A Levitical city (Josh 21:14) and a refuge of David (1 Sam 30:27).

socoh-hill.name: Socoh
socoh-hill.id: A hill-country Socoh distinct from the Shephelah Socoh of v. 35; possibly Khirbet Shuweiket near Yatta. Identification uncertain.

maon.name: Maon
maon.id: Tell Maʿin south of Hebron, the wilderness of Maon where David hid from Saul (1 Sam 23:24-25).

carmel-judah.name: Carmel
carmel-judah.id: Khirbet el-Karmil south of Hebron, distinct from Mount Carmel. Site of Nabal's farm and David's wooing of Abigail (1 Sam 25).

ziph-hill.name: Ziph
ziph-hill.id: Tell Zif southeast of Hebron. The wilderness of Ziph is a recurrent setting of David's flight from Saul (1 Sam 23, 26).

halhul.name: Halhul
halhul.id: Modern Halhul north of Hebron. The toponym is preserved unchanged.

beth-zur.name: Beth Zur
beth-zur.id: Khirbet et-Tubeiqa north of Hebron on the Jerusalem-Hebron road. Major Maccabean fortress (1 Macc 4:29).

gedor.name: Gedor
gedor.id: Khirbet Jedur north of Halhul. Distinct from other Gedors (cf. 1 Chr 4:39).

middin.name: Middin
middin.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the wilderness of Judah. Some have proposed Qumran-area sites (Khirbet Mird, Khirbet Qumran itself) for these otherwise unknown wilderness towns.

secacah.name: Secacah
secacah.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the wilderness of Judah. Some have proposed Qumran-area sites (Khirbet Mird, Khirbet Qumran itself) for these otherwise unknown wilderness towns.

nibshan.name: Nibshan
nibshan.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the wilderness of Judah. Some have proposed Qumran-area sites (Khirbet Mird, Khirbet Qumran itself) for these otherwise unknown wilderness towns.

city-of-salt.name: City of Salt
city-of-salt.id: Unidentified Judahite town in the wilderness of Judah. Some have proposed Qumran-area sites (Khirbet Mird, Khirbet Qumran itself) for these otherwise unknown wilderness towns.

en-gedi.name: En Gedi
en-gedi.id: The oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, with abundant springs in an otherwise arid coast. Tel Goren preserves Iron Age settlement; the cave-strongholds figure in David's flight from Saul (1 Sam 24).

luz.name: Luz
luz.id: Older name of Bethel (Gen 28:19, 35:6). Most readers take Luz and Bethel as the same place; the boundary description here ('from Bethel to Luz') has been read as moving from the sanctuary to the settlement just beside it, or as preserving an older twin-site memory.

archites.name: Archites
archites.id: A clan-zone on the Joseph border south of Bethel; Hushai the Archite was David's counsellor (2 Sam 15:32). No specific town; the pin marks the area between Bethel and Ataroth-Addar.

japhletites.name: Japhletites
japhletites.id: A clan-zone on the southern boundary of Joseph between the Archites and Lower Beth-Horon. No specific town; otherwise unknown.

ataroth-addar.name: Ataroth Addar
ataroth-addar.id: Often located at Khirbet ʿAtara south of Bethel. The simple form 'Ataroth' in vv. 2 and 7 is generally taken as the same site, though some have suspected a separate Jordan-valley Ataroth at v. 7.

michmethath.name: Michmethath
michmethath.id: A boundary feature 'before Shechem' (17:7), likely a ridge or pass on the line dividing Ephraim from Manasseh. Khirbet Makhneh el-Foqa east of Shechem has been proposed; not securely located.

taanath-shiloh.name: Taanath Shiloh
taanath-shiloh.id: Khirbet Tana el-Foqa (or el-Tahta) east-southeast of Shechem, on the descent toward the Jordan valley. Eusebius mentions a Thena ten Roman miles east of Neapolis, supporting the identification.

janoah-ephraim.name: Janoah
janoah-ephraim.id: Khirbet Yanun (modern Yanoun) southeast of Nablus. Distinct from the Galilean Janoah of 2 Kgs 15:29.

naarah.name: Naarah
naarah.id: Generally located at Khirbet el-ʿAuja et-Tahta or Tell el-Jisr in the Jordan valley north of Jericho. The same place is called Naaran in 1 Chr 7:28; a sixth-century synagogue mosaic was discovered nearby in 1918.

brook-of-kanah.name: Brook of Kanah
brook-of-kanah.id: Wadi Qana, draining westward from the central hill country to the Yarkon and the Mediterranean. The natural border between Ephraim (south) and Manasseh (north) through the Sharon Plain. Pin sits in the central wadi.

shechem.name: Shechem
shechem.id: Tell Balata at the eastern edge of modern Nablus, in the saddle between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. The patriarchal sanctuary of Gen 12:6, 33:18-20 and the covenant-renewal site of Joshua 24. Excavations by Sellin and Wright revealed Middle and Late Bronze fortifications and a fortress-temple.

en-tappuah.name: En Tappuah
en-tappuah.id: The spring associated with Tappuah (Sheikh Abu Zarad), serving as a boundary marker in v. 7. Some readers identify En-Tappuah with Tappuah itself; others take it as the spring below the town. Pin reuses Tappuah's coordinates.

beth-shean.name: Beth Shean
beth-shean.id: Tel Beth-Shean / Tell el-Husn at the eastern end of the Jezreel valley, where it descends to the Jordan. Major Egyptian administrative center in Late Bronze (governor's residence and temples excavated). The Philistines hung Saul's body on its walls (1 Sam 31:10). Hellenistic-Roman Scythopolis lay on the lower terrace.

ibleam.name: Ibleam
ibleam.id: Khirbet Belameh just south of Jenin, guarding the southern approach to the Jezreel valley. Site of Ahaziah's death-flight from Jehu (2 Kgs 9:27).

endor.name: Endor
endor.id: Generally located near the Arab village of Indur on the northern slope of the Hill of Moreh, with Khirbet Safsafa as the leading archaeological candidate. The medium consulted by Saul on the night before his death (1 Sam 28).

valley-of-jezreel.name: Valley of Jezreel
valley-of-jezreel.id: The broad alluvial plain between the Carmel ridge (south-west), the Galilean hills (north), and the Gilboa range (south-east). The natural east-west corridor between the coastal plain and the Jordan valley. Site of repeated battles in Israel's history.
